description: Typed current result families that an artifacts/** description asserts as registered while current-result-registry.json carries no result_kinds[] row for them. The gate tools/artifact_lint:asserted_result_families_are_registered refuses any such name that is not listed here, so this file is the visible ledger of assertions that outran the registry. Entries must identify the live specification report that owns closure and the exact missing contract; a listed family that becomes registered or loses every assertion is itself an error.
adjudication: Opened 2026-09-19 with the gate. chris adjudicated on 2026-09-19 that artifacts/** descriptions are a normative surface, which is what makes an assertion here a registration claim rather than commentary. Seven names were asserted and none was registered. did_core_id was not a family at all -- the sentence meant that organization_id is a did_core_id -- and was rewritten to name the family it actually intends. mimi_room_binding and moderation_franking_proof were registered in the same batch because their subject and their value were both fully determined by the payload schema. The four below are not deletable and not mechanically derivable: each needs one design decision that the descriptions do not contain, so each is listed with the exact missing decision rather than guessed at. Do not add an entry to defer work that is derivable. Reviewed again on 2026-09-19 by reading the whole spec rather than the descriptions alone. Two of the four reasons below were wrong and are replaced: the recorded blocker had been dissolved by prose that the entry never consulted, and in both cases a different, sharper blocker was found in its place. Correcting a reason is not adding or removing a name, so the ratchet still holds: the set of listed families may only shrink. Emptied on 2026-09-19 after reading the pre-migration history instead of the current tree. Every one of the four blockers recorded above was an artefact of one commit that deleted the registry those descriptions were written against, leaving each assertion standing with nothing under it: object_redaction's value was a whole-payload set with uniqueItems and its preserve[] items are Event Envelope top-level field names, pinned by the redaction fixture's preserved_fields vector, and several redactions on one object deliberately accumulate with no ordering rule -- so the elements never merge and the missing repeat-redaction rule was never needed; it is registered as keyed_set_add. organization_discovery and organization_moderation_policy were two independent whole-value families all along and are registered as such. view_reconcile was never a family: models/views.md section 3.2 is normative that all three View kinds write ONE family named for the View, its table survived the migration verbatim, and the name is registered as view. policy_rule never had a registry row in any version; its description rested on a state model that v1 does not have, so the assertion was deleted rather than registered, and the one Policy family, written whole by ak.policy.set, is registered as policy. The ledger is now empty. It stays in the tree because the gate reads it: an empty unregistered_families is the statement that no description outruns the registry, and the ratchet still forbids adding a name. Followed on 2026-09-19 by deleting the ak.policy.rule Event kind itself for the same reason the assertion went: it carried no policy_id, so its rule_id resolved to nothing, and editing a rule submits the whole authorized Policy document through ak.policy.set. The one Policy action family, policy_action, is registered separately by ak.policy.action.
current_review: The 2026-09-19 full artifacts/** scan supersedes the earlier two-file census. The remaining assertion maps to an active no-result_writes kind owned by the open 0650 coverage report. This row is an exact temporary owner, not permission to add unrelated assertions; rsvp and strand_watch were removed as soon as their typed result contracts became active.
